descripcion_es: Pollution, energy, recycling and climate change.
resumen: Vocabulary for talking about environmental problems, their causes and possible solutions, also useful in debates and essays.

explicacion.texto: “Medio ambiente” is the environment (with the). Many words in this field are uncountable: pollution, waste, rubbish, energy, litter. It is worth learning collocations: reduce emissions, cut down on plastic, run out of resources.

filas: the long-term rise in the Earth's temperature (es: cambio climático / calentamiento global)
dirty or harmful substances in air, water or land / to make them dirty (es: contaminación / contaminar)
gases that trap heat in the atmosphere (es: gases de efecto invernadero)
We must cut greenhouse gas emissions.
carbon dioxide released into the air (es: emisiones de carbono)
The plan aims to reduce carbon emissions.
coal, oil and gas used as fuel (es: combustibles fósiles)
Coal and oil are fossil fuels.
energy from sources that do not run out (es: energía renovable)
Spain produces a lot of renewable energy.
panels that turn sunlight into power / a group of wind turbines (es: placas solares / parque eólico)
They installed solar panels on the roof.
things people throw away (es: residuos / basura)
to use materials again / the process of doing so (es: reciclar / reciclaje)
rubbish dropped in the street or a public place (es: basura tirada en la calle)
Don't drop litter in the park.
an animal or plant that may soon disappear (es: especie en peligro de extinción)
The Iberian lynx is an endangered species.
a long period without rain / a large amount of water covering dry land (es: sequía / inundación)
the increase in the height of the sea (es: subida del nivel del mar)
Sea level rise threatens coastal cities.
not harmful to the environment (es: respetuoso con el medio ambiente)
that can continue without damaging the environment (es: sostenible)
the amount of CO₂ a person or activity produces (es: huella de carbono)
to use less energy (es: ahorrar energía)
Turn off the lights to save energy.
to use or consume less of something (es: reducir el consumo de)
We should cut down on plastic.
to use all of something and have none left (es: agotarse, quedarse sin)
We are running out of fresh water.
to get rid of something you do not want (es: tirar (a la basura))
plastic made to be used once and thrown away (es: plástico de un solo uso)

items: Environment takes the when it means nature: protect the environment.
Spanish “contaminación” is pollution; contamination is used mainly for dangerous substances in food or water.

ejemplos.frase: Air pollution in big cities is a serious health problem.
ejemplos.traduccion: La contaminación atmosférica en las grandes ciudades es un grave problema de salud.

ejemplos.frase: If we keep using fossil fuels, global warming will get worse.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si seguimos usando combustibles fósiles, el calentamiento global empeorará.

ejemplos.frase: Our town recycles more than half of its waste.
ejemplos.traduccion: Nuestra ciudad recicla más de la mitad de sus residuos.

ejemplos.frase: Many farmers are suffering because of the drought.
ejemplos.traduccion: Muchos agricultores lo están pasando mal por la sequía.

ejemplos.frase: Taking the train instead of the plane reduces your carbon footprint.
ejemplos.traduccion: Coger el tren en vez del avión reduce tu huella de carbono.

ejemplos.frase: Some experts fear we will run out of fresh water.
ejemplos.traduccion: Algunos expertos temen que nos quedemos sin agua dulce.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: In this sense environment takes the.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: There are a lot of pollutions in Madrid.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: There is a lot of pollution in Madrid.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “renovable” is renewable; energy is usually uncountable.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: Throw the papers to the rubbish.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: Throw the papers in the bin / away.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “tirar a la basura” is throw away or throw in the bin.

ejercicios.frase: We should cut ___ on single-use plastic.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the collocation from the second table, “cut down on”, which means “consume less of”. The clue is that cut and on are already there: what is missing is the middle particle of this three-part phrasal verb, which is down. The result is “cut down on single-use plastic”. It is a very common expression when talking about habits: cut down on sugar, cut down on driving.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To consume less of something is cut down on.
ejercicios.traduccion: Deberíamos reducir el consumo de plástico de un solo uso.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Cut off means “cut, disconnect” and is not combined with on; to consume less is cut down on.
Cut out means “remove completely”; also, it is not followed by on.
A calque of Spanish “consumir menos”: “cut less on” does not exist; the particle is down.

ejercicios.frase: At this rate, the planet will run ___ of natural resources.
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the phrasal verb from the second table, “run out of”, “use up, have none left”. The clue is the preposition of after the gap: run ___ of can only be completed with out. The result is “the planet will run out of natural resources”, with the subject that has none left and the complement after of. If the subject is what runs out, you say it without of: “Natural resources are running out”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To use up completely is run out of.
ejercicios.traduccion: A este ritmo, el planeta se quedará sin recursos naturales.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Run off means “escape, run away” or “drain away” and is not used with of.
Run away means “escape”; it does not express running out.
“Run short of” (“have too little of”) exists, but it does not mean using something up completely, which is what the card practises with run out of.

ejercicios.frase: Eating less meat can reduce your carbon ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “carbon footprint” (es: “huella de carbono”). The clue is the instruction and the word carbon: footprint literally means “the mark of a foot” and is used figuratively for each person's environmental impact. The result is “reduce your carbon footprint”, with the possessive your because it is each person's own footprint.
ejercicios.traduccion: Comer menos carne puede reducir tu huella de carbono.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Print means “printing, pattern”; the fixed word is footprint.
Track means “trail, path”; it does not form the collocation with carbon.
Trace means “mark, sign”; the expression is always carbon footprint.

ejercicios.frase: The giant panda is no longer classified as an ___ species.
ejercicios.explicacion: The first table includes “endangered species” (es: “especie en peligro de extinción”). The clue is the article an before the gap, which requires a word beginning with a vowel sound, and the word species. Endangered is an adjective formed from danger. The result is “an endangered species”; remember that species is the same in the singular and the plural.
ejercicios.traduccion: El panda gigante ya no está clasificado como especie en peligro de extinción.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Dangerous means “causing danger”, not “in danger”; also, it would need a, not an.
Extinct means “no longer existing”, already gone; it is not the same as endangered.
Endanger is the verb (“put in danger”); before species you need the adjective endangered.

ejercicios.frase: Wind and solar power are ___ sources of energy.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “renewable energy” (es: “energía renovable”). The clue is that wind and sun do not run out, so the source is renewable; in English the adjective is renewable, formed from renew. The card warns about the typical mistake of copying Spanish “renovable”, which does not exist in English. Fossil would be the opposite: coal and oil.
ejercicios.traduccion: La energía eólica y la solar son fuentes de energía renovables.

por_opcion.renewable: Correct. Renewable means that it regenerates; it is the adjective for wind and sun.
por_opcion.renovable: Incorrect. It is the Spanish word copied; it does not exist in English, where it is spelt renewable.
por_opcion.fossil: Incorrect. Fossil is used for coal, oil or gas (fossil fuels), which are not renewable.

ejercicios.frase: Coal, oil and gas are ___ fuels.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “fossil fuels” (es: “combustibles fósiles”). The clue is the list coal, oil and gas, which are the classic fossil fuels. In English fossil is spelt with double s and no final e, and here it works as an invariable adjective before fuels. Green, “ecological”, would be exactly the opposite.
ejercicios.traduccion: El carbón, el petróleo y el gas son combustibles fósiles.

por_opcion.fossil: Correct. Fossil fuels are coal, oil and gas.
por_opcion.fossile: Incorrect. It is a spelling mistake influenced by French or Spanish; in English it is fossil.
por_opcion.green: Incorrect. Green means “ecological, environmentally friendly”; coal and oil are exactly the opposite.

ejercicios.frase: There's too much ___ in the city centre because of the traffic.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that pollution is uncountable and is the word for air pollution, while contamination is used mainly for dangerous substances in food or water. The clue is “too much”, which only goes with uncountable nouns, and “because of the traffic”, which points to air pollution. That is why only pollution is correct, in the singular and without an article.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Pollution is uncountable and is the word for air pollution.
ejercicios.traduccion: Hay demasiada contaminación en el centro de la ciudad por el tráfico.

por_opcion.pollution: Correct. Pollution is uncountable, goes with too much and refers to air pollution caused by traffic.
por_opcion.pollutions: Incorrect. Pollution is uncountable and has no plural; also, too much requires an uncountable noun.
por_opcion.contaminations: Incorrect. Contamination is used for dangerous substances in water or food and is not usually plural either.

ejercicios.frase: People who drop ___ in the street can be fined.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table defines litter as “rubbish dropped in the street”. The clue is the collocation “drop ___ in the street”: drop litter is exactly the antisocial act of throwing paper or cans on the ground. Waste is more general and garbages does not exist, because garbage is uncountable. So the answer is litter.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Rubbish dropped in the street is litter.
ejercicios.traduccion: A quienes tiran basura en la calle pueden multarlos.

por_opcion.litter: Correct. Litter is rubbish dropped in the street or in a public place; drop litter is the usual collocation.
por_opcion.waste: Incorrect. Waste means waste materials in general (industrial, household) and is not used with drop in the street.
por_opcion.garbages: Incorrect. Garbage is the American word for rubbish and is uncountable, so it cannot take -s.

ejercicios.frase: Governments must do more to protect environment.
respuestas: Governments must do more to protect the environment.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that environment takes the when it means nature: protect the environment. The clue is the verb protect followed directly by the noun with no determiner, which is not possible here in English. Adding the article gives “protect the environment”. It is a common mistake because, as it is a general concept, learners tend to leave out the article as with other abstract nouns.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los gobiernos deben hacer más para proteger el medio ambiente.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Governments must do more to protect environment.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: environment, in the sense of nature, needs the.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Governments must do more to protect the environments.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The environment as a general concept is singular: the environment.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Governments must do more for protect the environment.
errores_previstos.explicacion: A calque of Spanish “para proteger”: purpose with a verb is expressed with to + infinitive, not with for.

ejercicios.frase: The river suffered several floodings last year.
respuestas: The river suffered several floods last year.
The river flooded several times last year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “drought / flood” (es: “sequía / inundación”), and the explanation of the correction states that a flood as a countable event is flood. The clue is several, which requires a plural countable noun: several floods. Flooding exists, but it refers to the phenomenon as an uncountable noun and is not usually made plural. You can also rephrase with the verb: “The river flooded several times”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A flood as a countable event is flood.
ejercicios.traduccion: El río sufrió varias inundaciones el año pasado.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The river suffered several floodings last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: flooding is uncountable; for countable events use floods.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The river suffered several flood last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Several requires the plural: floods.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The river suffered several inundations last year.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Inundation exists but is very formal and rare; the everyday word is flood.

ejercicios.frase: We must do less carbon emissions.
respuestas: We must produce fewer carbon emissions.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card stresses learning collocations such as reduce emissions, and the table gives the example “reduce carbon emissions”. The clue is the verb do, a calque of Spanish “hacer”: in English emissions are reduced (reduce, cut) or produced (produce), never “done”. Also, “less” with a plural is incorrect; to compare, you say fewer. So reduce, cut or produce fewer carbon emissions are all correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: Debemos reducir las emisiones de carbono.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We must do less carbon emissions.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: do does not combine with emissions.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We must make less carbon emissions.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Make is not the collocation either; also, with a plural you say fewer, not less.

errores_previstos.respuesta: We must produce less carbon emissions.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Produce is correct, but emissions is a countable plural and needs fewer; less is heard in speech, but the standard requires fewer.

respuestas: Turn off the lights to save energy
Turn the lights off to save energy
To save energy turn off the lights
To save energy turn the lights off
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “save energy” (es: “ahorrar energía”), with the example “Turn off the lights to save energy”. It is an imperative, with no subject, followed by purpose with to + infinitive. The phrasal verb turn off allows the object after the particle (turn off the lights) or in the middle (turn the lights off), so both answers are correct. The purpose can also go first: To save energy, turn off the lights.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Save energy means using less energy.
ejercicios.traduccion: Apaga las luces para ahorrar energía.

errores_previstos.respuesta: To save energy turn the off lights
errores_previstos.explicacion: The particle off cannot go between the article and the noun: turn the lights off or turn off the lights.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Turn off to save the lights energy
errores_previstos.explicacion: This mixes up the two phrases: the object of turn off is the lights and the object of save is energy.

ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes “recycle / recycling” (es: “reciclar / reciclaje”), with the example “Do you recycle glass?”. It is a present simple question, formed with the auxiliary do before the subject and the bare infinitive after it. Glass is uncountable and has no article because we are talking about the material in general.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Recycle means using materials again (es: reciclar).

errores_previstos.explicacion: The auxiliary do goes at the beginning of the question, before the subject.
The subject you goes between the auxiliary and the verb: Do you recycle.
This is an emphatic statement (“you really do recycle”), not a question; in the question do goes before you.

ejercicios.frase: Cycling is a cheap and ___ way to get around.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “sustainable” (es: “sostenible”). The clue is that the adjective goes with cheap and describes an environmentally friendly means of transport, as in the example “sustainable transport”. It is spelt with -ain- and -able: sustainable, formed from sustain (“support, maintain”).
ejercicios.traduccion: Ir en bici es una forma barata y sostenible de desplazarse.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is the Spanish word; in English it is sustainable.
A spelling mistake influenced by Spanish; it is spelt sustainable.
Sustained means “continuous, kept up” (sustained growth); it does not mean sustainable in the environmental sense.

ejercicios.frase: Please don't ___ away those bottles; we can recycle them.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table includes “throw away” (es: “tirar (a la basura)”). The clue is the particle away after the gap and the idea of getting rid of something instead of recycling it. Only throw away has that meaning. Take away and put away exist, but they mean “remove, take with you” and “put back in its place”; remember also the alternative “throw in the bin”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: To get rid of rubbish is throw away.
ejercicios.traduccion: Por favor, no tires esas botellas; podemos reciclarlas.

por_opcion.throw: Correct. Throw away means “put in the bin”, exactly the opposite of recycling.
por_opcion.take: Incorrect. Take away means “remove, take with you” (or food to take away), not put in the bin.
por_opcion.put: Incorrect. Put away means “put back in its place, tidy away”, the opposite of getting rid of something.

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the basic vocabulary for talking about environmental problems, their causes and their solutions: pollution, climate change, renewable energy, waste and recycling. It is a recurring topic in debates, essays and exam conversations. Spanish speakers find it difficult because many words are uncountable (pollution, waste, energy), there are false friends (renovable, contamination) and there are many phrasal verbs such as cut down on or run out of.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of the environment in English: the problems (pollution, global warming, drought, flood), their causes (fossil fuels, carbon emissions, deforestation) and the solutions (renewable energy, recycling, sustainable transport). It includes collocations and phrasal verbs used in fixed ways, such as reduce emissions or cut down on plastic.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is one of the most frequent topics in oral and written exams, because it lets you give opinions and argue. A mistake in number (pollutions) or a false friend (renovable, editorial) immediately reveals your level. Mastering the collocations makes your speech sound natural rather than translated.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is useful for commenting on the news, proposing measures, describing personal habits (I recycle glass) or debating public policy. The signals are topics such as climate, energy or waste. Spanish speakers tend to leave out the in “protect the environment”, to make uncountable nouns plural and to copy Spanish “hacer emisiones”; English says reduce or cut emissions.
